cases.case_text:

  Image Description: Biopsy revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis of the epidermis overlying a conglomerate of dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle in the upper dermis, partly showing thrombosis.

  Result: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant.

cases.case_text:
A woman in her 50s with stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma with metastases of the liver, lungs, and peritoneum (primary site unknown). cases.case_text:
A 65-year-old woman presented with blurry vision in her right eye for several months. Ocular history included 3 recurrent episodes of bilateral iritis occurring during 5 months, amblyopia in the left eye, and bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens. Patient had undergone left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior and had been on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years. Medical history and past medication use were otherwise unremarkable.

Visual acuity: 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS without improvement on pinhole testing. Intraocular pressures were normal. Right eye showed trace conjunctival injection without definite ciliary flush, 2+ fine keratic precipitates, and 1+ cells in the anterior chamber. Left eye had a few keratic precipitates. Dilated fundus examination revealed cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye and an epiretinal membrane in the left eye. No inflammation in the periphery was noted in either eye.

- Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT):  Image Title: OCT Scans  Image Description: Right eye showed significant cystoid macular edema and subfoveal fluid. Left eye had a mild epiretinal membrane.- Fluorescein Angiography:  Image Title: Fundus Fluorescein Angiography  Image Description: Revealed cystoid macular edema with leakage in both right and left eyes.- Blood Tests: Tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders were within reference limits. Normal findings for tick-borne and bacterial diseases.- Imaging:  Computed tomography of the chest was unremarkable.

B. Anastrozole-associated uveitis with cystoid macular edema

cases.case_text:

source_options.D: Type I cryoglobulinemia associated with multiple myeloma

cases.case_text:
A woman in her 80s with a history of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease presented with purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet. She was initially admitted for altered mental status in the setting of an unwitnessed fall and was noted to have 'bruises' on her lower extremities. New lesions developed on her nose, ear, and the extensor surfaces of her arms bilaterally.

The patient's nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear (helical rim and antihelix) were found to have dusky purpuric macules and patches. Her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms had reticulated purpuric macules and patches. There was skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows and knees.

- Laboratory tests:     - Hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL)    - Acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL)    - Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear    - Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses    - Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis    - Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels (cryocrit, 16%)    - Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies  - Biopsy findings:    Four-millimeter punch biopsy specimens from left ear, right arm, and forehead showed multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation  - Imaging studies:    CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions      - Bone marrow biopsy:    Hypercellular marrow consisting of 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction

A. Type I cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
B. Multiple myeloma
C. Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
D. Type I cryoglobulinemia associated with multiple myeloma
